summary.headline: Syrma SGS Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 67% YoY to Rs 1,604 crore and PAT rose 112% to Rs 106 crore; FY27 guidance of 35%+ growth reaffirmed and possibly exceeded.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was Rs 1,604 crore (+67% YoY), with operating EBITDA of Rs 162 crore (+69%, 10.1% margin) and PAT of Rs 106 crore (+112%). Growth was led by consumer ramp-ups, exports (+61% to about Rs 387 crore) and ODM (Rs 270 crore, about 115% YoY but down sequentially from Rs 345 crore in Q4). Management attributed the quarter to normal run-rate business rather than one-time items, and said supply-chain constraints (PCB chemicals, component lead times) led to a deliberate build in inventory, pushing net working capital days from 63 to 71. Management reaffirmed 10.5-11% full-year EBITDA margin guidance and said FY27 revenue growth would be 35%+, with a view to exceed guidance.

financial_highlights.change: approx +115% YoY; down from Rs 345 crore in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Rs 122 crore; cash and investments above Rs 800 crore
financial_highlights.change: short-term borrowings up about Rs 340 crore in quarter

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 90 crore (of which about Rs 50 crore on PCB project)

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: Largest vertical at 34% of business mix; growth from faster customer ramp-ups and front-loaded schedules. Management guides about 30% of annual revenue, with quarterly variation.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: About 25% of business mix (about one-fourth of revenue); growth driven by EV penetration and charging infrastructure. Five new auto clients onboarded in the quarter.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Sequentially moderated; ex-defence/maritime it was about Rs 325 crore vs about Rs 320 crore last quarter (Rs 460 crore total last quarter including about Rs 140 crore defence/maritime). Smart metering slowed, and maritime is second-half loaded.

segments.name: Healthcare / MedTech
segments.commentary: Healthcare order book about Rs 500 crore. Syrma Johari MedTech did about Rs 210 crore last year and is expected to grow about 50%. Target 7-8% of total business.

segments.name: IT and Railways
segments.commentary: Together about 9% of order book; management said IT business is growing at a fast pace, including server motherboard work under a C-DAC approval.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 35%+, with management expecting to exceed guidance based on Q1.
Full-year operating EBITDA margin guided at 10.5-11%; consumer-mix seasonality may put the full-year figure in the 30-32% range for that segment, per management.
Exports expected to grow 30-40% in FY27, taking exports to about Rs 1,500-1,600 crore (FY26: about Rs 1,200 crore).
ODM share target of 17-19% in the short term, with a long-term aim of 25%.
Growth of 30-35% expected to continue in FY28 and FY29, per management.
Net working capital elevated for at least the next quarter or two as inventory is held as a strategic asset.
New clients onboarded in the quarter may add more than Rs 1,000 crore of revenue at full ramp-up, with volumes starting next year.
capex_capacity: PCB project: building about 65-70% complete; equipment from October onwards; power-on January-March 2027; commercial production expected by April 2027. Phase 1 cost about Rs 400 crore, of which about Rs 130 crore funded so far.
PCB economics: asset turn about 1.5x at full utilisation; year-one utilisation 40-50%, rising to 80%+. EBITDA 15-18% at full ramp ex-PLI, and about 10% or lower in the initial year.
Ex-PCB capex guided at Rs 100-150 crore for FY27; about Rs 40 crore spent in Q1.
Current capacity utilisation 65-70%. Expansion underway at Bangalore and Pune, and a new MedTech facility at Jodhpur with plastic injection moulding and SMT lines.
Phase 1 PCB funding: 50-60% debt, plus a 50% government capex subsidy; Phase 2 and 3 expected to start around end-FY27 or early FY28.
Kaga JV (Syrma 60%, Kaga India 40%): initial investment about Rs 24-25 crore combined; opportunity estimated at Rs 300-500 crore over 3-5 years.
demand_pricing: Order book about Rs 6,770 crore at June end (about Rs 6,400 crore at March end); about Rs 5,400 crore to execute in the next 12 months; average execution period about 10-10.5 months. Q1 order intake about Rs 1,781 crore.
Order book mix: automotive about 29%, consumer about 30%, industrial about 24%, healthcare about 7%, IT and railways about 9%.
Customer concentration: top 5 about 38%, top 10 about 51%, top 20 about 66% of revenue.
18 new clients onboarded in Q1 (5 auto, 3 industrial, 2 healthcare, rest telecom, IT and railways).
Pass-through of memory and component cost increases: management said absolute margin rupee amounts are unaffected but percentage margin would dip as there is no markup on pass-through cost.
Exports by geography: USA about 22%, Europe about 40%, rest other countries; North America including Mexico and Canada adds about 15 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any one-time revenue booking in Q1, and what is the outlook for the next three quarters, especially consumer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no one-time transaction in the quarter; numbers are normal run-rate, with consumer up from about 30% to 34% of mix and the gain absorbed by exports and ODM growth. No quarterly outlook number was given; management said it does not view numbers quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Board resolution for a roughly Rs 1,000 crore QIP a specific fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it is an annual enabling resolution taken at the AGM, with no immediate need; management framed it as a war chest for opportunities such as semicon.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs 400 crore PCB Phase 1 need external funds, and how will Phases 2 and 3 be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 cost about Rs 400 crore, of which about Rs 130 crore is funded so far; 50-60% debt is planned, plus a 50% government capex incentive. Funding is from internal accruals, subsidies, debt and a treasury balance above Rs 800 crore. Phases 2 and 3 start around end-FY27 or early FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What asset turn and EBITDA margin should be expected for the PCB plant in its first year, ex-PLI?
qa_highlights.answer: Asset turn about 1.5x at full utilisation, with year-one utilisation of 40-50% rising to 80%+. EBITDA is 15-18% at full ramp ex-PLI and about 10% or lower initially. The 1-1.5x asset turn is on a gross basis, before subsidies.

qa_highlights.question: Given order book growth and the Rs 1,604 crore quarter, should the current run rate be extrapolated or will revenue accelerate? Is the 10%+ margin the floor at a 33-34% consumer mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 10.5-11% full-year EBITDA margin. Order book rose to about Rs 6,770 crore from about Rs 6,400 crore, with Q1 intake of Rs 1,781 crore. Q4 operating EBITDA margin was 11-11.3% versus 10.1% now; the full-year consumer-driven margin may be 30-32%, with seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 guidance be exceeded, and how much pass-through of memory and component inflation would hit margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects to exceed the 35%+ revenue guidance, with the size left to another quarter. On pass-through, absolute rupee margin is unaffected but percentage margin dips because there is no markup on pass-through costs. It did not quantify the full-year inflation impact.

risks_watch: Supply-chain constraints (specialty PCB chemicals, component lead times, West Asia geopolitics) could slow execution; management said a war room was set up and guidance is still held.

Working capital: net working capital days rose from 63 to 71, short-term borrowings rose about Rs 340 crore in the quarter, and management expects elevated inventory for at least the next quarter or two.
Sequential softness in ODM (Rs 270 crore vs Rs 345 crore in Q4) and industrial ex-defence/maritime (about Rs 325 crore vs Rs 320 crore); smart metering slowed and maritime is second-half loaded.
PCB project execution: about 65-70% building complete, power-on targeted January-March 2027, commercial production by April 2027, with ramp-up EBITDA initially about 10% or lower.
Margin dilution from pass-through of memory and component cost inflation, since no markup is earned on pass-through costs.
Customer concentration: top 5 about 38% and top 10 about 51% of revenue.
Watch next quarter: whether the company raises the 35%+ growth or 10.5-11% margin guidance, export run-rate (Rs 1,500-1,600 crore target), and the consumer share (about 30% annualised).
key_quotes: So, what we are focused on in Syrma SGS is to ensure that our customers don't suffer because of these supply chain constraints.
We have also taken a cautious call that we will not treat inventory as a working capital, at least for the next quarter or two.
I will answer the first question in an affirmative that there has been no one-time transaction which has been booked into the quarter.
So, we are very confident of scaling up this business and have a positive growth in the current year.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, exports, ODM and guidance, with management saying it expects to exceed the 35%+ revenue guidance. It was more cautious on supply chains and geopolitics, and on the quarterly margin and working capital path, which it framed as seasonal or temporary.

New MedTech facility at Jodhpur with plastic injection moulding and SMT lines

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 35%+ (held, with view to exceed), backed by a Rs 6,770 crore order book (about Rs 5,400 crore executable in 12 months), 18 new clients in Q1 and PCB Phase 1 (Rs 400 crore) due for commercial production by April 2027.
